findings.summary: GPU n-gram speculation shortened Census OCR to 15.03 s. GPU 3 emits about 1.60 tokens per verification step and still controls the tail.
observations: The accepted speculative configuration keeps four L4 GPUs, server concurrency eight, region window 64, dynamic pages, compiled BF16 embeddings and the same frozen OCR settings. One warm-up, three ordinary calls and a separate instrumented full call completed.

Median diagnostic call time is 15.77 s: OCR 15.027 s and embedding 0.622 s. Mean shares are 95.4% OCR and 3.9% embedding. The preceding non-speculative Census profile measured 24.597 s of OCR; full evaluator p95 changed from 25.299 to 15.862 s.

GPU 3 accepted 5,340 of 35,616 proposed tokens over the ordinary calls: 15.0% acceptance and 1.60 tokens per verification step, including the bonus token. Other GPUs averaged 1.02–1.15 tokens per step. These are counter differences across the diagnostic window, not isolated per-request rates.

OCR-window mean GPU busy for GPUs 0–3 is [9.1, 16.6, 6.1, 96.5]%, with [44, 44, 45, 45] one-second samples. GPU 3 averages 69.6 W under the unchanged 72 W limit. The other GPUs still finish much of their work before the tail; this does not establish peak compute or memory-bandwidth saturation.
The long page-5 region still produces 3,252 tokens and ends with EOS. All four bounded traces were captured and the complete instrumented output passed the frozen reference check.

The preceding Attention profile showed 1,510 generated tokens on GPU 3 versus 454 on GPU 1 despite nearly equal region counts. This motivates testing how regions are assigned after confirming the small pooled-p50 gain.
findings.next_step: Two proposals worsened the evaluator metrics and eight was effectively flat. Retain four and test shared region admission, with a round-robin control at the same capacity, to address the unequal GPU token work.
findings.optimization: Use image-derived work estimates to distribute regions while restoring reading order. Proposal depth is another controlled lever; acceptance is concentrated on the long Census sequence, so additional proposals may add overhead elsewhere.
